title: The Reformed dispute over indifference can likewise be settled
source_text: XXIII. Indidem quoque apparet facile componi posse dissidium quod adhuc superesse videtur inter Doctores Scholae Reformatae: dum alii, scilicet, affirmant libertatem arbitrii includere quandam agentis liberi indifferentiam, per quam positis omnibus ad agendum praerequisitis, potest agere, vel non agere, hoc aut illud agere; alii vero negant talem indifferentiam libertate includi, aut ad libertatem omnino pertinere.
pass_a_gloss: From the same source it appears also that the dissension can easily be composed which still seems to remain among the Doctors of the Reformed School: while some, namely, affirm that liberty of choice includes a certain indifference of the free agent, by which, all things prerequisite to acting being posited, it can act, or not act, do this or that; but others deny that such indifference is included in liberty, or pertains to liberty at all.
pass_b_english: The same considerations show that the disagreement still apparently left among teachers of the Reformed School can easily be settled.

Some of them hold that freedom of choice includes a certain indifference in the free agent, by which, given everything required beforehand for acting, it can act or not act, and do this or that. Others deny that any such indifference is included in freedom or has anything to do with it.

lemmas.gloss: all things prerequisite to acting being posited

choices.why: Kept as the Schools' technical term; Le Blanc fixes its sense as a real power to act otherwise, not a state of balance between options.
